sections.content: history[i] is an object that has .action and .frame. My legend function was receiving f.frame, but I was passing h (the history entry) — so it should be h.frame. I wrote legend(h.frame) — no wait, I wrote legend(h.frame) inside the loop… let me check: `print(i, h.action, legend(h.frame), box(h.frame))`. And legend(f) executes f.frame.ascii — that's wrong, f is already a frame. Fix: use f.ascii directly.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def legend(f):
    a = f.ascii.split('\n')
    s = a[58]
    out=[]; i=0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] not in 'cc':
            j=i
            while j<len(s) and s[j] not in 'cc': j+=1
            out.append(s[i:j][0]); i=j
        else: i+=1
    return out
def box1(f):
    a = f.ascii.split('\n')
    s=a[29]; out=[]; i=0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] not in 'cc':
            j=i
            while j<len(s) and s[j] not in 'cc': j+=1
            out.append(s[i:j]); i=j
        else: i+=1
    return [c[0] for c in out if c[0]!='R']
for i in range(0, 32):
    h = history[i]
    print(i, h.action, legend(h.frame), box1(h.frame))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
